text: hey everybody I've commented a lot on how we translate the Hebrew of Genesis 1 1 that there is one feature of this verse that I have not commented on much
and that's the fact that there is a word in the Hebrew of Genesis 1 1 that we never translate into English it is
always left untranslated and that is the word ET which is spelled aleph Tav with a cycle Under The Olive and we don't
translate it because we don't need to and we can't because it is a direct object marker and it is there to
indicate that what follows after is the direct object of the verb that precedes it and we don't use direct object
markers in English we have other ways to indicate what the direct object of the verb is and there are other ways that
other languages do it for instance in case-based languages you have the accusative case to Mark a word as the
direct object of a verbal action and so we don't really lose anything by not translating it and we couldn't really translate it to the begin with it would
only cause confusion if we tried to ensure it was somehow represented in Translation now another thing to note is that while this word is spelled using
the first and the last letters of the Hebrew alphabet there's not really significance to that as far as we can
tell the authors of the biblical text and the audiences among whom those texts originally circulated did not find
significance to this direct object marker containing the first and the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet and the
idea that this is the Alpha and the Omega the first and the last is something that is mostly brought up by Christians who are trying to find
significance in some of the occurrences of this word which occurs almost 11 000 times throughout the Hebrew Bible and
good luck to anybody trying to read significance into every single one of those occurrences so that is a contemporary renegotiation of what's
going on in the text that's an attempt to try to read significance and meaning into the text that was not going through
the heads of any of the authors of the biblical texts or any of its original audiences
